Summary answers:
- Prompts: median ~90 tokens, 75th ~150, heavy context tasks up to 800 tokens (rare).
- Responses: median 120 tokens, p95 ~400 tokens when long-form generation kicks in.
- Normal RPS: 35 RPS across cluster during business hours (US); typical concurrency ~420 reqs/min.
- Peak surge: we observed 9x sustained spikes for ~6–12 minutes after our email digests — absolute peak ~310 RPS for short windows, global bursts hit ~520 RPS for a few minutes during marketing pushes.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 450ms for short responses; for long-form we can tolerate up to 1.2s p95 but prefer optimized routing.
- We prefer synchronous serving for user-facing flows; async for batch jobs.
- KV cache: we can allow warm-start and are comfortable with prefix caching between sessions.

Thanks for the data, Ava. I pulled the CSV and sketched an initial sizing approach. High-level notes below — this is an early sketch, ballpark numbers only:

Sizing rationale:
- Baseline: 35 RPS steady => ~2.1M tokens/min at median token sizes (prompt+response). With average concurrency and latency SLO p95 450ms, target baseline capacity of ~6 concurrent inference workers per GPU for a 32GB quantized 7B variant.
- Surge handling: For 9x surge tolerance we recommend a hybrid approach: reserved pool sized for 2x baseline and an autoscale burst pool (pre-warmed instances + fast fallback to hosted API) to cover the remaining burst capacity. This avoids over-reserving while hitting SLOs.
- GPUs: Recommend NVIDIA H100x2 or equivalent for highest throughput on long-form; for 7–13B models a 48–80GB LLM-optimized instance (quantized) provides best cost/perf. For cost-sensitive routes, plan a mixed fleet with 4x cheaper A100/80GB quantized nodes for background tasks.
- Quantization: 4-bit quant (GPTQ-style) for inference routes acceptable to Heliox yields 2.5–3x throughput improvement and reduces memory footprint for KV cache.

Ballpark cost (monthly committed, US region):
- Reserved baseline pool (2x steady): estimated 6 x H100-equivalent nodes => $85k/month (committed).
- Burst buffer/autoscale (pay-as-you-go expected): variable, estimate $10–25k/month depending on burst frequency.
- Additional: SRE warmup automation + cache pre-warming runbook (one-time integration) ~ $12k professional services.

Operational notes:
- Nightly cache warmup: schedule low-cost batch runs to pre-fill hot prefixes 30–60 minutes before business hours; this reduces cold-start tail latency.
- Canary/rollout: use canary routing for long-form model variant to limit quality regressions during scale.

Next steps:
1) Dev/infra to validate GPU SKUs and expected concurrent warm workers per SKU (Dev, can you run perf test with their CSV sample?).
2) If validated, we'll prepare a concise one-page TCO and an optional pricing ladder (reserved tiers + burst).
3) Set follow-up on Wednesday with Heliox product and infra (Maya/Sam), propose 30 min + infra deep-dive.

Attachment: initial_proposal_estimate.pdf (sketch)
